instructions: Wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them 1/4 inch thick. Slice the onion and the bell pepper. Finely chop the ginger.
Put the peppercorns, fennel seeds, cumin seeds and coriander seeds in a mortar or spice grinder. Grind them coarsely and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mustard seeds, dried chilies and curry leaves. After about 20 seconds the seeds will pop. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.
Add the ginger and onion and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until the onion is soft.
Add the mushrooms and turn the heat to high. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until they've released their liquid and it has cooked off.
Add the bell pepper and cook for 2 minutes, until it's just tender.
Add the ground spices and the salt. Stir for 1 minute, until every slice is coated.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. The chilies stay whole, so lift them out for anyone who wants it milder.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen (the lead, 5.0 from 187 ratings) and Swasthi's Recipes (4.98 from 88) both cook mushrooms and bell pepper with a coarsely ground pepper, fennel and cumin mix and curry leaves; the lead also adds coriander seeds and dried red chilies. Green Bowl 2 Soul adds lime juice and ginger-garlic paste. Hebbar's uses ghee, swapped for oil to keep this vegan. The pepper is cut to 2 tsp for 1 lb of mushrooms (the lead's ratio would be about 1 1/2 tbsp) to keep the base mild.
